what: ggsmatr: Example using the iris dataset
title: ggsmatr example
text: presence fitted SMA lines ggplot2 scatter plot can obtained object created smatr::sma(). first read example data included package fit common-slope SMA group.
code: datafile <- system.file("iris.csv", package = "ggsmatr") df.iris <- read.csv(datafile, encoding = "UTF-8")  fit <- sma(   Sepal.Length ~ Sepal.Width + Species,   data = df.iris,   shift = TRUE,   elev.test = TRUE,   alpha = 0.05 ) ggsmatr(   data = df.iris,   groups = "Species",   xvar = "Sepal.Width",   yvar = "Sepal.Length",   sma.fit = fit ) +   theme(legend.position = "top", legend.title = element_blank()) +   ylab("Sepal.Length") +   xlab("Sepal.Width") #>        group    r2  pval #> 1     setosa 0.551 0.000 #> 2 versicolor 0.277 0.000 #> 3  virginica 0.209 0.001 #> Warning: Using `size` aesthetic for lines was deprecated in ggplot2 3.4.0. #> ℹ Please use `linewidth` instead. #> ℹ The deprecated feature was likely used in the ggsmatr package. #>   Please report the issue to the authors. #> This warning is displayed once per session. #> Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was #> generated.

title: ggsmatr example
text: Given SMA lines pass group centroid, presence parametric confidence ribbon can added ci = TRUE. ribbon related slope confidence intervals already stored sma() fit (Slope_lowCI Slope_highCI), related OLS band geom_smooth(). confidence level one used model fitted, example sma(..., alpha = 0.05) 95% intervals. According Warton et al. (2006, 2012) limits obtained inverting one-sample test SMA slope, ggsmatr() maps onto plot. fitted line constrained pass group mean (xbar, ybar), slope intercept independent. presence slope interval therefore converted family lines centroid: pmin() pmax() required, lower slope produces higher line x < xbar. envelope pinches group mean fans toward ends observed x range. presents slope-CI envelope, bootstrap prediction band pointwise CI E[Y | X]. numerical intervals can inspected smatr object:  Transparency smoothness ribbon can controlled ci.alpha n:
code: y_low  <- ybar + Slope_lowCI  * (x - xbar) y_high <- ybar + Slope_highCI * (x - xbar) ymin   <- pmin(y_low, y_high) ymax   <- pmax(y_low, y_high) fit$groupsummary[, c("group", "Slope", "Slope_lowCI", "Slope_highCI")] #>        group    Slope Slope_lowCI Slope_highCI #> 1     setosa 0.929894   0.7665449     1.128053 #> 2 versicolor 1.644914   1.2882605     2.100306 #> 3  virginica 1.971740   1.5274522     2.545258 ggsmatr(   data = df.iris,   groups = "Species",   xvar = "Sepal.Width",   yvar = "Sepal.Length",   sma.fit = fit,   ci = TRUE ) +   theme(legend.position = "top", legend.title = element_blank()) +   ylab("Sepal.Length") +   xlab("Sepal.Width") #>        group    r2  pval Slope Slope_lowCI Slope_highCI #> 1     setosa 0.551 0.000 0.930       0.767        1.128 #> 2 versicolor 0.277 0.000 1.645       1.288        2.100 #> 3  virginica 0.209 0.001 1.972       1.527        2.545 ggsmatr(   data = df.iris,   groups = "Species",   xvar = "Sepal.Width",   yvar = "Sepal.Length",   sma.fit = fit,   ci = TRUE,   ci.alpha = 0.15,   n = 150 )

what: How the confidence ribbon is calculated
title: Ggsmatr
text: ribbon OLS interval geom_smooth(se = TRUE), obtained combining intercept CIs slope CIs independently. SMA (MA) lines constrained pass group centroid (x‾,y‾)(\bar{x}, \bar{y}), slope intercept related : elevation y‾−bx‾\bar{y} - b\,\bar{x}. smatr::sma() already constructs confidence intervals slope inverting one-sample slope test (Warton et al. 2006, 2012). limits stored sma.fit$groupsummary Slope_lowCI Slope_highCI. confidence level one used model fitted, example sma(..., alpha = 0.05) 95% intervals. Given presence fitted SMA line centroid, ggsmatr() maps slope interval family lines point. group xx along observed range: ylow=y‾+blow(x−x‾),yhigh=y‾+bhigh(x−x‾) y_{\mathrm{low}}  = \bar{y} + b_{\mathrm{low}}(x - \bar{x}), \qquad y_{\mathrm{high}} = \bar{y} + b_{\mathrm{high}}(x - \bar{x}) ymin ymax taken pmin() / pmax(), lower slope produces higher line x<x‾x < \bar{x}. resulting envelope pinches group mean fans toward ends line. Users can inspect numerical intervals : ribbon presents therefore parametric slope-CI envelope. include separate intercept band, bootstrap prediction interval, pointwise CI E[Y∣X]E[Y \mid X] ordinary least squares. ribbon can tuned ci.alpha (transparency) n (number x values evaluated group):
code: fit$groupsummary[, c("group", "Slope", "Slope_lowCI", "Slope_highCI")] ggsmatr(   data     = df.iris,   groups   = "Species",   xvar     = "Sepal.Width",   yvar     = "Sepal.Length",   sma.fit  = fit,   ci       = TRUE,   ci.alpha = 0.15,   n        = 150 )
